sources.locator: "Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II", revision 1376254812, "Siege of Cusco"

explanation: The rebellion's article, opening its "Siege of Cusco" section, gives the march on the city as a decision taken to hold what had been won: **"Seeking to maintain the advantages gained at Quiquijana, Sangarará, and Lampa, he decided to anticipate the enemy and go on the offensive."** The sentences on either side put the same thing in order — Túpac Amaru returned to Tungasuca on 17 December, "the rebel leader began preparations for the great expedition against Cusco", and the army departed on 20 December. `enabled` and not `caused`, because Sangarará is one of three advantages the sentence names and the article gives no weight to any of them; what the source supports is that the victory was part of the position from which the offensive was launched, and not that it brought the offensive about.
